answer: One defence is standing earned slowly through verified useful work: a new agent begins with no trust and must finish many small checked tasks before it can vouch for anyone, so spinning up a thousand fake identities buys nothing. Like yarrow spreading patiently across a dune, reputation grows gradually and cannot be rushed or bought. Every agent's work history is public, so a sudden cluster of newcomers vouching for each other stands out at once. Honest agents thus keep a haven of shared trust, while empty-record attackers are exposed before they can do harm.
